notes: `upstream` is the Isol8 PAPERCLIP FORK image (ghcr.io/isol8ai/paperclip, built by the fork's own CI from branch isol8/2026.8-circuit-breaker, tag v2026.8-isol8.2), pinned by DIGEST. v2026.8-isol8.2 REBASED the whole patch stack onto upstream master f554d6737 (2026-08-05). The branch was renamed from isol8/2026.7-circuit-breaker, which is deliberately left unmoved at c9d68063 as the pre-rebase rollback ref. What the rebase brings: DEFAULT-OPEN VISIBLE ISSUE WRITES (upstream #10804) — an agent that can read a company-visible issue may now comment on it, update its fields, create children, and assign it, replacing the narrow ownership/mention grants that previously denied every cross-agent write. Before this, `issue:mutate` had no permission-key mapping and no manager clause, so decideBase fell through to deny_unsupported_action, and the CEO/manager `tasks:manage_active_checkouts` override in assertAgentIssueMutationAllowed was UNREACHABLE (the coarse boundary check runs first) — that is why Friday, seeded role="ceo", got a 403 trying to close a Jarvis-owned task. The assignee run-lock while an issue is `in_progress` survives, and the checkout override now sits above it. Also in: governed interaction addressees (migrations 0203/0204), cross-task write attribution + audit receipts + actionable denials (#10843), contained cross-issue side effects (#10837), the maintained in_review review-path contract (#10675), heartbeat shared-workspace serialization, and the decisions/queues feature (0197-0202). Rebase surgeries to know about: our routine-circuit-breaker migration was renumbered 0197 -> 0209 (upstream now owns 0197-0208) with the journal `when` held at 1784300000000 so already-migrated DBs skip it — re-verified against drizzle-orm 0.45.2's migrator, which reads max(created_at) ONCE before the loop and applies an entry only when that value is below its folderMillis, so our low `when` is skipped on dev/prod (whose max is upstream 0196's 1785170001001) while a fresh DB still gets it in journal order; the SQL is IF NOT EXISTS as a second guard. COMPANY_DELETE_SEQUENCE was extended to cover the eleven new decisions/secret-proposal tables, which hold NO ACTION references to companies/agents/issues/heartbeat_runs/agent_api_keys and would otherwise 500 DELETE /api/companies/:id again (decision_effect_executions is deliberately excluded: no company_id, emptied by cascade from decisions). The fork's docker.yml also needed a lowercase step for upstream's new registry-backed BuildKit cache — buildx rejects the capitals in `Isol8AI/paperclip`. NEW fork patches carried forward from isol8.8: accepted-interaction requeue backoff and the productivity-review stale sweep. Carried patches, all still real source on the fork: the routine circuit breaker, the agent-delete routines-FK fix, honest run-log workspace/session-reset lines for cloud-adapter runs, the 400 guard on non-UUID X-Paperclip-Run-Id headers, complete child-row cleanup on issue delete, the agent-comment whitespace fix, the resilient detached agent.wait (<=5-min slices across the API Gateway 2h WS cap, 48h ceiling), the FK-safe company delete (COMPANY_DELETE_SEQUENCE), daily-cap retry parking, the PAPERCLIP_SKIP_BUILTIN_AGENTS gate (Isol8 tenants get exactly Friday+Atlas; wired in paperclip-stack.ts), and the bundled isol8.notifications forwarder (approval.created/resubmitted + agent.run.finished/failed -> backend /webhooks/paperclip-events; unconfigured instances no-op). The extended Dockerfile is a thin passthrough that re-tags this image into ECR so per-tenant ECS tasks can pull it with execution-role creds (the fork GHCR package is private; the build authenticates with GITHUB_TOKEN and the package grants Isol8AI/isol8 read access). `extendedImage` + per-env `dev.tag`/`prod.tag` are the ECR-published extended image deployed to dev/prod — merging a digest bump here builds the extended image, and its tag is then bumped into `dev.tag` (validate) and `prod.tag` (promote) in follow-up PRs. `upstreamCommit` is the FORK commit (drives the extended tag). Bump `upstream` here to the fork's new digest when shipping fork changes.
